newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland sees terms of trade down in '97, up in '98.
newsitem.headline: Finland sees terms of trade down in '97, up in '98.

text.p: Finland's terms of trade are expected to weaken this year with import prices rising and export prices falling, but the terms of trade would improve in 1998, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.

"Growth in Europe is accelerating after a year-long slack phase," the ministry said. "Stronger growth in Europe is supporting Finnish exports which are expected to grow 5.6 percent in volume this year," it said.
"Growth in forest industry exports is expected to rise nine percent as demand recovers and the supply of exports increases," it said.
But in the metal and engineering industries, growth in exports would be "only a good three percent" due to the low volume of shipbuilding orders.

"Many product groups in both the metal industry and the forest industry are burdened with weak export prices, and average export prices for the whole year are expected to fall slightly short of last year," the ministry said.
"With import prices rising, the terms of trade will weaken by a few percent," it added.
Finland's trade and current account surpluses would be lower in 1997 than last year. @
In 1998, however, both the trade and current account surpluses would probably be higher "as the terms of trade are expected to improve," it said.

"Further stable international economic growth is expected in 1998. Finland's competitiveness will remain at about the current year's level so the prospects for further export growth are good," the ministry said.
In the new forecast, the 1997 GDP growth figure was raised to 4.6 percent from 3.9 percent last September. Next year, GDP growth would be "almost four percent," it said.
